verdict.rationale: Temporal itself provides recurring Schedules that start Workflow Executions at set times, not just one-off runs. Those workflows run on workers with automatic retries and crash recovery, and the docs position it for orchestrating AI agents; a community user independently confirms Schedules work like a more flexible cron. Automations must be written as code, and some users report workflows stuck 'In Progress' with buried errors, which tempers how autonomous they are. Missing for 10: a no-code or low-code way to set up automations, and stronger evidence that unattended runs surface failures reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: A Schedule contains instructions for starting a Workflow Execution at specific times.
If an Activity fails, Temporal automatically retries it based on your configuration.
If the process running it crashes, the Temporal Service hands the work to another process, which rebuilds the state of the execution and resumes at the point where it stopped
there's a Schedules feature that allows you to periodically start a workflow, like a cron but more flexible.
Orchestrate your workflows, AI apps, and agents across any models, tools, systems, and length of time.
